basis: CSX publicly established the decline by October 19, 2023. Its consolidated income statement reports Q3 revenue of $3,572 million against $3,895 million for Q3 2022, down 8.29% and below the $3,700.25 million cutoff. The earliest date remains unverified. I recovered the opening exchange from CEO Joe Hinrichs’s September 6 TD Cowen session and the moderator’s account, but could not verify the complete Q&A. The upper_bound below is the reported actual.

coverage.detail: April 20, preceding earnings cycle. The $3.71 billion revenue and 9% growth were Q1 actuals. The release supplied no Q3 consolidated revenue range.

April 20, slide 20. The full-year outlook covered low-single-digit growth in revenue ton-miles, a volume measure, and an approximately $300 million decline in supplemental revenue. Neither establishes a Q3 total.
July 20, immediately preceding release. The $3.70 billion revenue and 3% decline applied to Q2. Management gave no numerical Q3 consolidated revenue ceiling.

July 20, slide 19. CSX retained full-year ton-mile guidance and expected larger year-over-year declines in supplemental revenue during the second half. The approximately $300 million estimate covered that revenue component for the full year.
July 20 call transcript. Kevin Boone’s Q3 mid-teens decline referred to coal revenue per unit compared with Q2. It supplies no numeric upper bound for consolidated year-over-year sales.
August 4, Exhibit 99.1 announced operations executive Jamie Boychuk’s departure.
CSX identified CFO Sean Pelkey as its August 15 Deutsche Bank conference speaker and announced a public webcast.

August 15, transcript copy. Analyst Amit Mehrotra suggested a mid-to-high-single-digit year-over-year revenue decline. Pelkey answered about coal revenue per unit, intermodal storage and pricing. He gave no consolidated endpoint and did not adopt the analyst’s estimate.
CSX’s August 31 wire announcement identifies the missing event precisely: Hinrichs at TD Cowen on September 6 at 9:10 a.m. Eastern. CSX announced a live webcast and replay through investor relations.
The issuer archive exposed year selectors but no retrievable September 2023 replay, transcript or CSX conference deck in the accessible page.
The conference-host URL returned the TD Securities homepage. It supplied no session materials.
A fellow participant’s official event page identified the webcast platform and conference code, WSW cowen140. Its webcast link was specific to Cummins.
I tested this candidate CSX replay path and the conference root https://wsw.com/webcast/cowen140/. Neither was accessible, and a targeted search did not verify a CSX-specific replay URL.

The indexed September 6 transcript preview contains moderator Jason Seidl’s opening question and part of Hinrichs’s answer about mixed freight demand. Opening the transcript returned a cache miss. The remainder of the Q&A was unavailable.
BamSEC lists the September 6 session and its revised transcript between the August 15 conference and October 19 results. Following the entry returned the index without the transcript text.
September 7, moderator Seidl and TD Cowen colleagues reported that CSX reaffirmed low-single-digit full-year revenue ton-mile growth. Their recap contains no Q3 consolidated revenue ceiling.

September 8, a contemporaneous account corroborates the annual ton-mile outlook and quotes Hinrichs’s closing remarks about staffing. Its quarter-to-date percentages measure freight volumes. It does not reproduce the full exchange.
September 6 Form 8-K disclosed the underwriting agreement for $600 million of notes due 2033. It supplied no conference transcript or Q3 sales forecast.
September 7 Form 8-K disclosed issuance of the notes. The dollar amount was debt principal.
September 8, Exhibit 99.1 announced Mike Cory’s appointment as chief operating officer. It supplied no sales outlook.
The prior review verified the September 21 notice scheduled results for October 19 and contained no preliminary figures. The issuer URL did not reopen in this audit.

October 19, Exhibit 99.2. The same consolidated GAAP revenue line gives $3,572 million and $3,895 million in the quarter columns for September 30, 2023 and 2022. The reported decline was $323 million.

publication_date_evidence: Exhibit 99.2 says CSX announced Q3 results on October 19, 2023. EDGAR records acceptance of the 8-K containing the release and financial tables on October 19 at 16:01:28, before the October 20 Form 10-Q. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/277948/000027794823000051/0000277948-23-000051-index.htm
